items.item: The form is split into titled sections (personal, job and contract, bank and tax, emergency contact, documents) in a single column, with a visible label above every field and no placeholder-only labels
items.evidence: SECTIONS render <section><h2> Personal details / Job and contract / Bank and tax information / Emergency contact, plus Documents. Every field has <label for> with block mb-1 above the input. Placeholders are only example values. Only two side-by-side pairs (first/last name, city/postal code); the rest is one field per row.

items.item: Required fields are marked consistently, and optional fields are labelled as optional or left unmarked by a stated convention
items.evidence: Header states '* Required'; required labels get ' *' and aria-required; optional fields (Reports to, Contract end date, Postal code, Social insurance, Contact email) are unmarked. Documents table uses * plus sr-only '(required)' and an 'Optional' status badge.

items.item: Field widths match their content: dates, postal codes and tax codes are narrow; inputs use the right types (email, tel, date)
items.evidence: dob/startDate/endDate w-40, postal w-28, taxCode w-56, dependants w-28, email max-w-xl. Types: type=email, type=tel, type=date, type=number; salary is a right-aligned text input with inputmode numeric.

items.item: An option to save the form as a draft is offered, and saving a draft does not demand every required field
items.evidence: #draftBtn 'Save draft' calls saveDraft(), which never calls validateAll(); it toasts 'Draft saved for <name>' and sets a 'Draft saved HH:MM' status.

items.item: Save and Cancel stay reachable while scrolling (a sticky bar or equivalent), Save is a verb label and is not disabled before submitting
items.evidence: The bar uses 'sticky bottom-0' inside <main overflow-y-auto>, but main has no fixed height (wrapper is min-h-screen). The page grows to 3279px and the document scrolls, so the sticky bar never pins to the viewport. The 1440x900 screenshot shows no action bar, and the full-page screenshot shows it only at the very bottom. Save is the verb label 'Create employee' and is enabled before submit, but the sticky requirement fails.

items.item: Fields validate on blur and on submit; with several errors a summary at the top links to each field and focus moves to the first invalid field
items.evidence: form 'focusout' handler calls validateField; submit() calls validateAll(); renderSummary() shows '<n> fields need attention' with <a data-jump> links when there are 3 or more errors, and submit() calls el.focus() on the first error. Inline errors use aria-describedby and aria-invalid.

items.item: Leaving the page with unsaved input triggers a warning
items.evidence: window 'beforeunload' handler when dirty; guard() opens the #leaveDlg dialog 'You have unsaved changes. Leave without saving?' for Cancel and nav links.

items.item: The document upload states accepted file types and the size limit, lists chosen files with a remove button, and is keyboard operable
items.evidence: Documents table has an 'Accepted type' column (PDF, JPG or PNG...) and the note 'Files up to 10 MB'. Uploaded rows show file name, size, and a 'Remove' <button> (aria-label 'Remove <doc>'). The actions are native buttons that trigger a hidden file input. The 10 MB limit is enforced in JS. The type is not enforced (no accept attribute).

items.item: Success is confirmed with a message that names the employee and is announced to assistive technology
items.evidence: submit() calls toast(`Employee ${first} ${last} (NV-0248) created`) into #toast, which has role=status (a live region present in the DOM before the update). The status badge also changes to 'Onboarding'.

notes: The audit score of 100 does not catch the sticky-bar failure, which comes from the layout (min-h-screen wrapper with an unconstrained overflow-y-auto main). Minor: the Documents table's Actions column is clipped at 1440 (the 'Download' button is cut off in the full-page screenshot). Date inputs show mm/dd/yyyy, which is a locale mismatch for a vi-VN product. The summary only appears with 3 or more errors. The Documents section is a table rather than a field list, which is acceptable. No template tells: no gradient (only the skeleton shimmer), no glass, no emoji, no KPI tiles, no greeting header, no navy sidebar; the initials avatar 'LH' is a real person.
